divergences.verdict: A or C. The modern established terms descend from the common Latin names that Xylander cites (quarta, quinta, octava; English fourth, fifth, octave), so the established term belongs on them, and the Greek names need a literal rendering (A) or a transliteration (C), as about.md §4.1 allows where a name is explained; both explain their departure from §4.2 in a note. B's and D's Russian invert the historical relation (diatessaron becomes «кварта», quarta becomes «четвёртая») but stay intelligible; D's English follows the opposite strategy to its Russian without comment; B's English loses the Greek names and with them the content of the sentence (major error below). The choice between literal and transliterated Greek names must agree with X29–X30 and X35. Literal glosses added to transliterated names in the running text go in square brackets (about.md §4.6), or into a note, since X29 explains the names at once. If transliteration is chosen, the note should warn that Russian «диапазон» is also the everyday word for 'range'.

divergences.verdict: about.md § 4.1 asks that the explanation of a name stay readable: the established term and the literal rendering side by side, or an explanation in a note. A does this in the running text, and its solution fits the function of the Latin best: Xylander glosses the Greek names by the names current in his own Latin (octava, quarta, quinta), which are exactly the modern established terms. D does the reverse (established terms for the Greek names, Xylander's Latin ordinals literally): acceptable, but «две восьмых» / 'two eighths' reads as the fraction 2/8. B renders both sets by the established terms; this follows § 4.2 but turns the 'hoc est' gloss into a tautology, explained only in its notes, and it departs from B's own solution in X28 and X35, where the Latin ordinals are rendered literally («четвёртой», «восьмая»). C keeps transliterations in the running text, a departure from § 4.2 for which it gives its reason in its X28 note (to keep Xylander's double naming visible); but transliterations are not terms a modern reader understands (§ 4.1), and Russian «диапазон» is the everyday word for 'range'.

Antiphonon is when high and low are consonant together at the same moment: as when the 8th note with the 1st, the 11th with the 4th, the 12th with the 5th, the 15th with the 8th rises or falls equally in raisings or lowerings, so that low notes answer to high, or vice versa, proportionally. The composition reading has the stronger support inside this text: Vinet uses conficere for making up an interval from its parts (V39 Conficitur autem Dia-tessaron duobus tonis et hemitonio …; V55 ex tribus intervallis Dia-tessaron intervallum confectum est) and for melos and modulationes (V32, V65); ex his naturally means the fifteen notes just listed (cf. L&S I.A.1 unde pallium conficiatur, making from a material); and Xylander's parallel (Per has sonorum species heccaedecachordum … absolvitur) expresses composition. Prefer composition; C's reading is a defensible minority construal, not an error. The doctrine is the same either way, so the final choice is the editor's.

by_translator.strengths: Exact and literal, with the most disciplined terminology: one rendering of intensio («напряжение» / 'tension') throughout both versions, Xylander's word pairs kept apart (ratio / proportio, concinnare / coaptare, coalitus / confundere), ratio names formed on the Boethian pattern where the Latin has them (super bipartiens tertias, X36). Its solution for Xylander's double naming of the intervals (Greek names rendered literally beside the established terms, X28–X30, X35) is the one the reviews prefer. Careful arithmetic, well-argued text proposals (7 judged sound), and notes on Xylander's and Vinet's characteristic words. 0 major and 12 minor errors; best base in 96 segments for Russian (16 alone) and 98 for English (12 alone); 67 notes recommended for the commentary.
by_translator.weaknesses: Literalism sometimes costs idiom: «удержание голоса» (X08), «звучащим при» (X32), «Это о звуках» (X17), 'dwellings' for mansiones (X57), 'eight cannot be squared' (V27), 'terminates through four' (V34). Twice it translates its own conjecture instead of the reading text (X24 propositi duplum, X38 quam), which belongs in the text issues. Two note claims are wrong or overstated (X15 on LSJ headwords; V24, where its Russian «её же» cannot keep the ambiguity it claims). The English of V05 mixes 'Universe' and 'universe'.

by_translator.strengths: Readable, natural prose in both languages, with some well-judged idiomatic solutions (the closing formula 'So much for notes', X17; 'the full pitch range of the double octave', V49, which the review prefers). Its readings of the arithmetic are correct, and its contextual renderings of intensio, though inconsistent, are each intelligible. 1 major and 36 minor errors; best base in 6 segments for Russian (0 alone) and 7 for English (0 alone); 6 notes recommended for the commentary.
by_translator.weaknesses: The only major error of the whole comparison: at X28 the English drops the Greek names diatessaron, diapente, diapason, which the sentence exists to gloss. Many minor faults of the same kinds: connectives left out (Enimvero, Caeterum, Porro, Verum, utique, horum), additions without brackets (eight sign errors: 'system', 'instruments', 'the ratio', 'proceed', 'steps'), paraphrase that flattens the Latin antitheses (X37, X57, V65), and the conjecture of X24 translated instead of the reading text. Terms: heccaedecachordum made a 'system' and Pentecaedecachordum a coined «пятнадцатиструнник» (X15); super bipartiens tertias paraphrased (X36); the pitch pair collapsed (X32); vis and facultates merged as 'capacity' (V49); intensio rendered five ways; Vinet's simplex merged with non-compositum and Xylander's incompositum; non tamen read as 'not yet' (X33). Few notes, and few worth keeping.

by_translator.strengths: The closest to the construction of the Latin and the most reliable: it renders the second quoque of X26, the idiom duae partes = two thirds (V42), the accusative of respect of X32, the adjectival paraphonon / antiphonon, and keeps Vinet's and Xylander's different words visible. Consistent terminology in both versions and in both languages, a single rendering of intensio, and the best notes of the four (doctrine, arithmetic, the page images, the translators' habits); its text proposals are the most often judged sound (8), and it argues and itself rejects the weaker alternatives in its doubts. 0 major and 3 minor errors; best base in 104 segments for Russian (22 alone) and 108 for English (18 alone); 82 notes recommended for the commentary.
by_translator.weaknesses: Its transliteration of the Greek interval names in X28–X30 and X35 is reasoned (note at X28) but «диапазон» misleads a Russian reader, for whom it means 'range' (X30). English 'genus' for the non-technical genus (X18) and 'modulation' for Xylander's modulatio (X44) invite confusion with the genera and with the modern sense; «меса единственная» / «меса одна» half-translate the qualifier of mese (X14, V17); an occasional calque («через один-единственный интервал», V32); one note claims an ambiguity that its Russian does not keep (V24).

by_translator.strengths: Fluent, modern Russian and English that read well on their own; a sound grasp of the doctrine and the arithmetic; some good idiomatic restructurings (X01) and legitimate alternative construals that the reviews accept (V44 scope of the negative, X30 relative quod); careful bracketing in places ('[of pitch]', '[ratio]' in English). 0 major and 35 minor errors; best base in 9 segments for Russian (0 alone) and 11 for English (0 alone); 17 notes recommended for the commentary.
by_translator.weaknesses: Freer than the brief allows: it regularly drops the connectives that carry Xylander's and Vinet's argument (Porro, Nam, Sed, Verum, enim, proinde, Caeterum, quin et … quoque, plane), flattens 'not … alone, but also' into a plain list (X57, V65), recasts the definition of the note as a relative clause (V11) and adds words without brackets (seven sign errors). In X28 its Russian and English follow opposite strategies without a note. Terms: the ratio name of X36 replaced by a description; materies as 'content' (X42), which hides the 'matter' of X43; vox, intensio, concinnare and genus / species rendered differently from place to place; hymenaeus and exodius described rather than named; literal «две восьмых» / 'two eighths' (X30). Two note claims are wrong (X04 on Xylander's reason for proportionalitas; V42 on the numerals of the figure).

overall.summary: Across the 124 segments the team recorded 32 divergences, 1 major and 54 minor errors and 24 editor questions for Xylander, and 29 divergences, 0 major and 32 minor errors and 24 editor questions for Vinet. All four translators understand both Latin versions and recompute every ratio correctly; no wrong number, ratio or ratio bracket was found in the running text of any of the four, and there is only one major error in the whole set (B's English at X28). The four fall into two pairs. A and C are close, literal and consistent: they keep the Latin's construction, its signs and its word pairs, and they are the best base almost everywhere (most often jointly, 'A = C'); C has the fewest faults and the most useful notes and is the best single base, A is close behind and often more exact in its terminology. B and D write freer, more idiomatic prose but leave out many of the connectives that carry the argument, add words without brackets, paraphrase antitheses and vary their technical terms; their Russian and English are rarely the best base, though individual phrasings are worth taking over. The decisions left to the editor are chiefly terminological: intensio ('tension' throughout, or 'pitch' in the definitions); how to render Xylander's double naming of the intervals (X28–X30, X35); proportio beside ratio in Xylander; the form of paraphonon / antiphonon; transliteration of the Greek compounds in X15 and of mese monos (X14); Vinet's simplex and melos; the name Exodius; and whether a translator's conjecture may ever stand in the running text (X24, X38). The term concordance recommends one rendering for each, consistent with about.md § 4, and lists twenty term inconsistencies, all minor, chiefly in B and D.
overall.contamination: none: no member of the team reported meeting forbidden material, and the assembler met none (only dictionary pages, Lewis & Short, were opened for the concordance).
